text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Chemicals concern DSM is to invest one billion guilders in takeover and expansion of German company Vestolen's polyolefin activites. (p1)
- Government asks public prosecutor to investigate IT companies' financial liability for the millenium bug. (p1)
- Dutch economy grows 3.3 pct in 1996 despite fall of 33 pct in foreign trade growth. (p1)
- Dutch cocoa association NCV lobbies for creating a bulk cocoa futures market in London. (p1)
- Media giant Polygram's 1997 first half results stable, due to dollar and sterling. (p2)
- KLM's U.S. partner Northwest Airlines net drops to $ 200.8 million from $ 256.2 in first six months of 1997. (p2)
- Temp agency Randstad abandons plans to set up mobile surgical teams for hospitals. (p3)
- Criminal activities in the Netherlands generated value added of about five billion guilders, or one pct of GDP in 1996, the Central Bureau of Statistics estimates. (p3)
- Philip Morris is not interested in taking over brewer Heineken for the next two years at least. (p21)
- KLM subsidiary Air UK sees 30 pct increase in passengers this year. (p23)
- Rabobank fears capital of some three billion guilders will be destroyed as a result of restructuring the pig breeding sector which has been hit by swine fever. (p1)
